requirement.summary: Vulnerability Issues - JWT Token Contains Sensitive Internal Infrastructure Information and Is Transmitted via URL
requirement.description:
Issue from: pentest-report-HQ-Pentest-env-1781148005691 1.pdf

Finding 6: JWT Token Contains Sensitive Internal Infrastructure Information and is Transmitted via URL Parameters

- Stop putting the report session token and callback address in the browser URL, so internal server hostnames are not visible in Network.

- When BIRT package is new enough (check version.txt: 1.1.11 Rev#290 or higher): the first open uses POST with rptSession / rptOrigin instead of URL query parameters.

- The session value starts with enc1. (encrypted). Later page flips / re-runs use cookies rptSes / rptOrg under /birt.

- If only PHP or only BIRT is upgraded, the other side still accepts the old parameter names, so mixed packages do not break report open.

- On failure, the screen shows a short message with Ref: …; details stay in server logs (birt_security / birt_api).

These functionalities involve:

- Auto reports

- Favorite reports

- Preset parameter reports

- Client-side reports

- Viewing reports after printing

QC Test Scope (Finding 6)

How to tell PHP / BIRT package version

- PHP (HQ Report plugin): use the package / build under test for this release.

- BIRT (Java report viewer): open BIRT version.txt. If it shows 1.1.11 Rev#290 or higher → new BIRT. If the version is lower → old BIRT.

Environment

- A — both new (main test): new PHP + new BIRT (version.txt has 1.1.11 Rev#290 or higher). This is the required full check.

- B — new PHP + old BIRT: version.txt is below 1.1.11 Rev#290. Only a quick check: open 1 report and confirm it still opens (compatibility).

- C — old PHP + new BIRT: PHP not yet upgraded, BIRT already new. Only a quick check: open 1 report and confirm it still opens (compatibility).

P0 — Must test (Environment A; sample 1–2 reports per entry)

- Standard HQ report preview (Reports listing → View): first BIRT request is POST; body has rptSession starting with enc1. and rptOrigin; no internal ELB / internal hostname on the URL; no plaintext jwt= / callbackUrl= on the URL; report renders.

- Favorite reports: open a favourite; same checks as above; report renders.

- Preset parameter reports: add preset from BIRT toolbar (no wrong_param_format); run report via preset; report renders.

- Client-side reports: open from POS/client; same checks; report renders.

- Viewing reports after printing: print / print queue then view result; report/print path works.

- Export: Excel/PDF download OK; Network URL must not contain duplicated frameset?__report=&https://.../frameset?__report=; Legacy CSV export succeeds (no The report file : does not exist or contains errors.).

- Pagination / second request: after open, cookies rptSes and rptOrg exist under /birt; flip page / re-run still works.

P1 — Recommended

- Error path: generic message + (Ref: xxxxxxxx), no internal hostname / stack in UI.

- Environments B and C: open one report each — report must still open (mixed package allowed).

P2 — Sample only

- Auto reports: one scheduled/manual run still succeeds (no browser JWT Network check required).

- Optional: one drill-down report; one EN + one ZH open.

Out of scope for full matrix

- Do not retest every POS/CUS/TMS report design.

- Do not retest report designer / ACL listing / unrelated modules.

Pass criteria (Environment A)

Browser Network shows no internal hostname and no plaintext JWT on first open; first request is POST with enc1. token; cookies work for follow-up; Favorite / Preset / Client / Print-view / Export checks above pass.
requirement.release_notes:
Bug Fixing: [HERO-68271] Fix the issue that report session token and internal server address are exposed in the browser URL when opening a report
Descriptions:
Fix the security issue that when a user opens a report in Infrasys Cloud, the report session token and callback address were passed in the browser URL. This could expose internal server hostnames in the browser address bar or Network panel.
After this fix, when both the Infrasys Cloud Report package and the BIRT report viewer package are upgraded together, the first open of a report no longer puts the session token or the callback address in the URL. The report still opens and works as before (preview, favorite, preset, client-side open, print view, export, and page flip).
If only one of the two packages is upgraded, report open remains compatible. The full security improvement (no token / internal hostname in the URL) applies when both packages are new. For the BIRT side, version.txt should show 1.1.11 Rev#290 or higher.
Configuration / Parameter:
No special configuration or parameter is required.
This case does not add any new report parameter or system setting. Both the Infrasys Cloud Report package and the BIRT report viewer package should be deployed for the full fix.
How to reproduce the issue (before fix):
1. Log in to Infrasys Cloud.
2. Open Report module and open any standard report (for example: Reports listing -> View).
3. Open the browser developer tools Network panel while the report viewer loads.
4. Check the first request to the report viewer.
Result before fix:
- The first request URL contains jwt and/or callbackUrl query parameters.
- The URL or token content may show an internal server hostname.
- The report can still open, but sensitive information is visible in the browser.
Field Definition:
This case does not involve field definition.
Result / Sample:
After fix (both packages upgraded; BIRT version.txt is 1.1.11 Rev#290 or higher):
1. Log in to Infrasys Cloud.
2. Open a standard report from Reports listing -> View.
3. Check the browser Network panel for the first report viewer request.
Expected result:
- The first request is a POST. The URL does not contain plaintext jwt= or callbackUrl=.
- No internal server hostname is visible on the report open URL.
- The report renders normally.
- Favorite reports, preset parameter reports, client-side reports, viewing after printing, Excel/PDF/CSV export, and page flip / re-run still work.
- If an error occurs, the screen shows a short message with a Ref code. No internal hostname or technical stack is shown to the user.
